chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman al-Azrami, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

The abandoned (child) is free. So when he grows older, if he so desires, he may choose as a guardian the one who picked him up, or else let him return the expenditure to him, and let him go and choose as a guardian the one whom he so desires.

key_terms.الْالْتِقَاطُ: Picking up or finding a foundling

ai.seo_question: What are the rights and options of a foundling child upon reaching adulthood in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic status of a foundling (al-manbuth) as free-born, granting them autonomy upon maturity to either remain with their caretaker by reimbursing expenses or to depart and choose their own guardian. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the intrinsic freedom of the individual and the contractual nature of custodial care, distinguishing it from permanent slavery. The ruling underscores the balance between the caretaker's financial investment and the child's right to self-determination.
